source: audio-tools model-policy review (MATURATION-PROGRAM.md Phase 4) plus vendor model cards; uncertain values are stated as uncertain in notes
notes: Model choice is data plus evidence. This seed declares static facts; the selector applies policy; the qualification harness promotes.
readiness=available means an adapter exists and the model is expected to run. candidate, experimental, and watch are honest non-runnable or unqualified states.
Only available records are default-eligible. A default candidate must also carry the default role; a merely available record is an alternative, not a default.

A non-available record with the default role must set allow_default=true, and availability still ranks first among default candidates, so an available promoted default is never displaced by an opt-in candidate.
provider_ids are stable health/lifecycle ids owned by internal/capabilities. engine_ids are STT stream-selection ids owned by internal/sttengine; non-STT records leave engine_ids empty.

For remote BYOK streaming providers and batch-only adapters, engine_ids is empty: they are chain-routed and do not participate in StreamConfig.EngineID selection until sttengine (and the provider catalog) declares a real engine.
WER is a percentage, SIM is a 0..1 similarity score, RTF is an x-realtime factor. Benchmark numbers are copied from the named source, not scenario-measured.
size_mb_approx=0 means the artifact size is not established in this seed; it is not a claim that the model is weightless.
Summarize records mirror resources/ollama/model-policy.json; a drift test fails when the summarize.default or chat.small model (or a declared fallback) has no record.

artifact names the resource data artifact that supplies local weights. A conformance test proves every readiness=available local model names a declared artifact, that the artifact the whisper resource pins for WHISPER_MODEL_PATH is the registry default for whisper-local, and that each capability's default fits the declared resource budget.

field_reference.name: human display name
field_reference.provider_ids: stable provider ids used for health, lifecycle, and settings (must appear in known_provider_ids)
field_reference.engine_ids: STT stream-selection ids (sttengine manifest ids for local engines); empty for non-STT records, BYOK/gateway/browser providers, and batch adapters with no engine
field_reference.runtime: execution backend (whisper.cpp | kyutai | sherpa-onnx | kokoro | onnxruntime | pytorch | vllm | byok | gateway | browser)
field_reference.artifact: resource artifact identity for local weights: {resource, name}; resource.json owns URL, checksum, size, and install layout. Required for readiness=available local runtimes.
field_reference.size_mb_approx: approximate primary artifact download size in MB; 0 = not established
field_reference.params: parameter count as published, or unknown
field_reference.commercial_use: yes | no | unknown; no and unknown require license_notes
field_reference.allow_default: explicit opt-in allowing a non-available record to carry the default role
field_reference.hardware: cpu_capable, gpu_required, min_vram_gb, min_ram_gb, os_arch (empty = no constraint)
field_reference.benchmarks: wer, sim, rtf, or notes; nil means not established

models.name: Whisper Medium (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19, same host and harness as the turbo receipt: canonical clip WER 0.00; 61-minute fixture 52.8 s wall (RTF 69.3x); Vulkan GPU residency 1,861 MiB. Retained as the rollback/comparison baseline, not as a broad quality claim.

models.notes: ggml-medium.bin is about 1.5 GB and is acquired on demand (group "medium-model") rather than installed with every resource. Batch-only in audio-tools; whisper.cpp declares no native streaming. It carries the quality role as the rollback/comparison model, not the default.

models.name: Whisper Large v3 (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: Quality tier only. Not promoted: CPU throughput and real-duration latency are unmeasured in this scenario.

models.notes: ~3.1 GB ggml artifact. The 6 GB VRAM figure is an operational comfort estimate, not a measured floor; CPU inference works but is slow.

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical clip WER 0.00; 61-minute fixture 30.3 s wall (RTF 120x); Vulkan residency 1,817 MiB. Quality tier; not a device matrix.

models.notes: ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin is the accuracy tier, not the shipped default. It is an on-demand artifact (group "turbo-model") because the resource-conscious default is whisper-small. Choose it when dictation accuracy matters more than ~1.3 GB of GPU/VRAM.

models.name: Whisper Small (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical 'the quick brown fox jumps' clip transcribed exactly (WER 0.00); warm wall 0.31 s for 1.95 s audio (RTF 6.3x). One clip on one host, not a dictation-quality or device-matrix claim.

models.notes: ggml-small.bin is the shipped runtime default (eager artifact): 488 MB on disk, about one third of turbo. It preserves multilingual support and passes the canonical quality clip exactly, while cutting the resident footprint enough to leave the GPU free for other work.

models.name: Whisper Base (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical 'the quick brown fox jumps' clip transcribed exactly (WER 0.00); warm wall 0.18 s for 1.95 s audio (RTF 10.5x). One clip on one host, not a dictation-quality or device-matrix claim.

models.notes: On-demand fast tier: 148 MB, about 3x less disk than small and faster on constrained hosts. Accuracy on real dictation is below small; use it only where footprint dominates.

models.name: Whisper Tiny (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical 'the quick brown fox jumps' clip transcribed exactly (WER 0.00); warm wall 0.16 s for 1.95 s audio (RTF 12.5x). One clip on one host, not a dictation-quality or device-matrix claim.

models.notes: On-demand edge tier: 78 MB. It transcribes clean speech acceptably but degrades quickly on accented, noisy, or long-form audio; it is not a dictation default.

models.name: Kyutai STT 1B (English/French, streaming)
models.license_notes: CC-BY-4.0 requires attribution and licence propagation.

benchmarks.notes: Native streaming only; no batch endpoint and no confidence signals. Date-stamped PROBLEMS entries show product-path latency is backend-bound after capture, so no latency claim is made here.

models.notes: GPU-required. The 8 GB VRAM figure is an operational estimate; the resource has not been qualified on CPU. Emits no confidence signals, so the egress hallucination signal stage is skipped for this engine.

models.notes: Candidate quality tier. The 16 GB VRAM figure is an estimate for the 2.6B checkpoint plus decoder overhead and is not measured on this host.

models.license_notes: k2-fsa publishes the sherpa-onnx toolkit and model exports under Apache-2.0.

models.name: Rumble 2 Flash (batch ASR, 45 languages)
models.license_notes: Apache-2.0 per the upstream model card.

benchmarks.notes: Open ASR Leaderboard English average WER 6.60; RTFx 6338. Batch benchmark only, not an audio-tools latency receipt.

models.notes: Batch ASR, not native streaming. Candidate default for local batch/multilingual work; allow_default is explicit so promotion is a seed decision backed by a receipt. engine_ids is empty until a real rumble engine/adapter exists in sttengine and the provider catalog. The vLLM adapter is GPU-oriented in practice, so CPU viability is not claimed even though the weights fit in CPU RAM. Artifact size ~1 GB is an estimate from 0.5B parameters.
